question: According to the manual, what has the greatest degrading effect on a rider's ability to think clearly and ride safely?
choice_c: Alcohol and other drugs, more than any other factor
explanation: Alcohol and other drugs, more than any other factor, degrade your ability to think clearly and to ride safely. As little as one drink can have a significant effect on your performance.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.35, 'Being in Shape to Ride'

question: The manual states that studies show what percentage of all riders killed in motorcycle crashes had been drinking?
explanation: Studies show that 40% to 45% of all riders killed in motorcycle crashes had been drinking.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.35, 'Why This Information Is Important'

question: Of the riders killed who had been drinking, the manual says only about how many had a BAC above the legal limit?
explanation: Only one-third of those riders had a blood alcohol concentration above legal limits -- the rest had only a few drinks in their systems, enough to impair riding skills.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.35, 'Why This Information Is Important'

question: The manual states that injuries occur in what share of motorcycle crashes that involve substance abuse, compared with 33% of similar automobile crashes?
explanation: Injuries occur in 90% of motorcycle crashes and 33% of automobile crashes that involve abuse of substances.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.35, 'Why This Information Is Important'

question: Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC), as defined by the manual, is:
choice_a: The number of drinks consumed in the last 24 hours
choice_b: A fixed value that is the same for every person
choice_c: The amount of alcohol in relation to blood in the body
choice_d: Only measured through a breath test, never blood or urine
explanation: Blood Alcohol Concentration or BAC is the amount of alcohol in relation to blood in the body.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.36, 'Blood Alcohol Concentration'

question: According to the manual, alcohol can generally be eliminated from the body at a rate of about:
choice_c: It cannot be eliminated at any measurable rate
explanation: Generally, alcohol can be eliminated from the body at the rate of almost one drink per hour, though other factors may also influence the level of alcohol retained.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.36, 'Blood Alcohol Concentration'

question: The manual lists three factors that play a major part in determining BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast you drink, and:
choice_c: The time of day you started drinking
choice_d: Whether you are riding alone or with a passenger
explanation: Three factors play a major part in determining BAC: the amount of alcohol you consume, how fast you drink, and your body weight.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.36, 'Blood Alcohol Concentration'

question: According to the manual's alcohol-content comparison, a 12-ounce can of beer, a mixed drink with one shot of liquor, and a 5-ounce glass of wine:
choice_a: Have wildly different alcohol content, with beer being weakest
choice_b: All contain the same amount of alcohol
choice_c: Cannot be compared in terms of alcohol content
choice_d: Only wine and beer are comparable; liquor is different
explanation: A 12-ounce can of beer, a mixed drink with one shot of liquor, and a 5-ounce glass of wine all contain the same amount of alcohol.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.36, 'Blood Alcohol Concentration'

question: In Pennsylvania, according to the manual, a rider is considered to be driving 'under the influence' if their blood alcohol level is:
choice_b: .15% or higher, only for a first offense
choice_d: There is no specific threshold in Pennsylvania
explanation: In Pennsylvania you are considered to be driving 'while under the influence' if your blood alcohol level is .08% or higher.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.37, 'Penalties for Driving While Under the Influence of Alcohol or Drugs'

question: For a first DUI conviction or acceptance into an Accelerated Rehabilitation Disposition (ARD) program, the manual says a rider could face all of the following EXCEPT:
choice_c: Being ordered into alcohol and drug rehabilitation treatment
choice_d: An automatic doubling of their motorcycle's registration fee
explanation: For a first conviction or ARD, penalties listed are: lose your license, be sentenced to jail, pay fines, and be ordered to undergo alcohol and drug rehabilitation treatment and/or Alcohol Highway Safety School -- not a registration fee increase.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.37, 'Penalties for Driving While Under the Influence of Alcohol or Drugs'

question: Under Pennsylvania's Implied Consent Law described in the manual, refusing to take a chemical test of breath, blood, or urine after a DUI arrest results in:
choice_a: An automatic one-year license suspension, in addition to any suspension for a DUI conviction
choice_b: No penalty as long as you are found not guilty of DUI
choice_c: A fine only, with no effect on your license
choice_d: A suspension only if you are also convicted of a second offense
explanation: If you refuse to take one or more chemical tests after a DUI arrest, your driving privilege will be automatically suspended for one year, in addition to any suspension imposed for a conviction or ARD.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.37, "Pennsylvania's Implied Consent Law"

question: According to the manual, a conviction for DUI combined with a refusal to take a chemical test could result in a total license suspension of:
explanation: Altogether, a conviction plus refusal could result in a two-year driving privilege suspension.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.37, "Pennsylvania's Implied Consent Law"

question: The manual explains that your license will be suspended for refusing a chemical test even if you:
choice_a: Only refused a breath test but agreed to a blood test
choice_b: Were not actually the one operating the motorcycle
choice_c: Are not found guilty of driving under the influence
explanation: Even if you are not found guilty of driving while under the influence, your driving privilege will be suspended for one year if you refuse to take a blood, breath, or urine test.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.37, "Pennsylvania's Implied Consent Law"

question: The manual warns that a drinking rider's ability to judge their own riding is affected first, meaning:
choice_a: They will always recognize when they are impaired
choice_c: They become more cautious than usual
choice_d: They may perform more and more poorly while thinking they are doing better and better
explanation: Your ability to judge how well you are riding is affected first. Although you may be performing more and more poorly, you think you are doing better and better -- the result is riding confidently while taking greater risks.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.37, 'Minimize the Risks'

question: The manual says that setting a drink limit or pacing yourself are poor strategies because:
choice_a: Judgment, one of the first things affected by alcohol, is needed to stick to the plan
choice_b: They work perfectly for experienced drinkers
choice_c: They are illegal under Pennsylvania law
choice_d: They only apply to riders under 21
explanation: Setting a limit or pacing yourself are poor alternatives at best -- your ability to exercise good judgment is one of the first things affected by alcohol, so you may not realize how much your skills have suffered.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.38, 'Make an Intelligent Choice'

question: One way the manual suggests protecting a friend who has had too much to drink is to:
choice_a: Let them decide on their own without interfering
choice_b: Serve them food and coffee to pass the time and keep them from riding
choice_c: Encourage them to ride slowly instead of not riding at all
choice_d: Wait for them to sober up before mentioning any concern
explanation: Keep them there -- use any excuse to keep them from getting on their motorcycle. Serve them food and coffee to pass the time, and explain your concerns for their risk of getting arrested or hurt.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.38, 'Steps to Protect Friends'

question: The manual notes that riding a motorcycle, compared to driving a car, is:
choice_a: Less tiring, due to the wind cooling the rider
choice_b: About the same in terms of fatigue
choice_c: More tiring, so you will tire sooner on a long trip
explanation: Riding a motorcycle is more tiring than driving a car. On a long trip, you'll tire sooner than you would in a car. Avoid riding when tired.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.38, 'Fatigue'

question: According to the manual, experienced riders seldom try to ride more than about how many hours in a single day?
choice_c: There is no practical limit for experienced riders
explanation: Limit your distance -- experienced riders seldom try to ride more than about six hours a day.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.38, 'Fatigue'

question: The manual recommends taking a rest break and getting off the motorcycle at least every:
choice_d: Rest breaks are unnecessary if you feel fine
explanation: Take frequent rest breaks -- stop and get off the motorcycle at least every two hours.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.38, 'Fatigue'

question: The manual warns that artificial stimulants used to fight fatigue often result in:
choice_a: Permanently improved alertness with no downside
choice_b: Extreme fatigue or depression when they start to wear off
choice_c: No effect on riding ability either way
choice_d: Improved judgment for the rest of the trip
explanation: Don't drink or use drugs -- artificial stimulants often result in extreme fatigue or depression when they start to wear off, leaving riders unable to concentrate on the task at hand.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.38, 'Fatigue'
